rationale: Evidence from the development runs: all 60 trials went off track (0 finishes). Progress stalled at 0.10 to 0.16, max_error was about 0.06 m (the off-track limit), and line_loss_events reached 1 to 2. Steering oscillation was 0.09 to 0.14. The main failure is that the five sensors span only ±0.02 m. Once the line drifts about 3 cm from centre, it leaves the sensor array, the robot loses the line, and it runs off. Signal scale is about x_line/0.02, so kp=2.5 gives a turn of roughly 2.5 per 2 cm offset, which is aggressive. The combined effect is overshoot and oscillation followed by loss. Changes: (1) Widen the sensor array to ±0.04 m (five sensors at -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04) so the line stays visible at larger offsets, and move the sensors to y=0.05 to give more lead. (2) Scale the weights to x/0.04, giving (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), so the signal stays in the same range. (3) Reduce kp from 2.5 to 2.0 to soften the overshoot. (4) Raise kd from 0.3 to 0.6 for more damping of the oscillation. (5) Reduce base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1 so the robot can track bends before it leaves the line. The cost is a slower lap, but the first goal is to finish and stay on the line. (6) Lower mass to 0.6 kg to reduce yaw inertia and improve response. Expected result: no off-track events on the oval and s-bend, fewer line-loss events, and oscillation below 0.1. The slalom may still be the hardest track. Next iteration: if max_error is still near 0.06 with few line losses, the cause is steering lag, so kd or kp needs more change. If line losses dominate, widen the array further or lower base_speed. Once the robot finishes, raise base_speed to meet the 1.5 m/s needed to complete within 3 s.
